subject: Food Science
title: Sourdough Fermentation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Sourdough Fermentation.

hook.text: San Francisco's most famous sourdough starter has been alive since 1849—fed daily for over 170 years.

buildup.text: Sourdough starters contain wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in symbiosis. The yeast raises the dough; bacteria add flavor.

discovery.text: Lactobacillus sanfranciscensis produces acetic and lactic acid—creating the signature tang that commercial yeast can't replicate.

twist.text: Sourdough bread has a lower glycemic index than white bread. Fermentation partially breaks down starches and gluten.

climax.text: Each starter has a unique microbial community shaped by local flour, water, and air. No two starters are identical.

punchline.text: A living culture of wild microbes, fed daily, making bread. Ancient biotech.

quiz.question: What makes sourdough different from commercial yeast bread?
options: Wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria create unique flavors and lower glycemic index
